question_text:
Pattern Matching with Wildcards

You are building a search filter for an advanced bioinformatics system. The system uses a special pattern language where:

* matches any sequence of characters (including an empty sequence).
? matches exactly one arbitrary character.

Given a pattern string P and a text string T, determine if the pattern matches the entire text. Output 1 if the pattern fully matches, and 0 otherwise.
explanation: This is solved with 2D DP. dp[i][j] = true if pattern[0..i-1] matches text[0..j-1]. Base: dp[0][0]=true; dp[i][0]=true only if all pattern[0..i-1] are '*'. Transition: if pattern[i-1]=='*', dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] (skip '*') OR dp[i][j-1] ('*' matches one more char). Else if pattern[i-1]='?' or equals text[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Time Complexity: O(M*N).
answer:
import sys

def solve(pattern, text):
    m, n = len(pattern), len(text)
    dp = [[False]*(n+1) for _ in range(m+1)]
    dp[0][0] = True
    for i in range(1, m+1):
        if pattern[i-1] == '*': dp[i][0] = dp[i-1][0]
    for i in range(1, m+1):
        for j in range(1, n+1):
            if pattern[i-1] == '*': dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] or dp[i][j-1]
            elif pattern[i-1] == '?' or pattern[i-1] == text[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]
    return "1" if dp[m][n] else "0"

if __name__ == '__main__':
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    pattern = lines[0].strip() if len(lines) > 0 else ""
    text = lines[1].strip() if len(lines) > 1 else ""
    print(solve(pattern, text))
